column3: The Hebrew states that one may not enter the king’s gate in sackcloth; BSB explicitly attributes the prohibition to the law.
The Hebrew says sackcloth and ashes were spread out for many; BSB describes many lying in them.
The Hebrew says they told her, without explicitly naming Mordecai as the subject of their report; BSB supplies his name.
The Hebrew asks what this was and why it was; BSB interprets the questions as asking what troubled Mordecai.
The Hebrew commands her to go to the king; BSB describes urging her.
The Hebrew says they reported Esther’s words; BSB uses a passive clause.
The Hebrew says not to think in her soul of escaping in the king’s house from among all the Jews; BSB explicitly supplies alone and the fate of the Jews.
The Hebrew emphasizes keeping silent by repeating the verb; BSB says remain silent.
The Hebrew introduces going to the king with “and so”; BSB says “After that.”
